rules.sentence: To manage patients with severe life-threatening bleeding, start by giving 10 mg of vitamin K intravenously, infused over 20 to 60 minutes, to prevent anaphylactic and anaphylactoid reactions.
Vitamin K requires 12 to 24 hours to become effective.
Clinicians can administer another dose if the INR remains high after 12 hours.
Awaiting laboratory and imaging results is unnecessary before administering vitamin K if severe bleeding is evident.
If anticoagulation needs to resume, clinicians can administer heparin while the patient remains resistant to warfarin.
